answer: Admission requires 1,000 distinct cryptographic nullifiers derived from a verifiable registry of non-transferable human-verified credentials. A verifier monitors the ocean of incoming transcripts, demanding a fresh proof per action. Like a zephyr moving through a willow grove, the verifier checks for duplicate keys; an honest agent pays for one credential, while 1,000 fakes must solve costly, non-batchable proofs. Violations result in a 60-day lock.
